authority.interpretation: The monolith remains the canonical issuer and durable refresh store. This wave closes caller-selected cross-client rotation in code; it does not enable the dormant identity service.

migration.legacyPolicy: Existing NULL client or family rows are never guessed, backfilled, or claimed. Runtime exact-client/family predicates reject them without mutation and force fresh authentication. Legacy logout revokes only the exact presented row. A separately reviewed enforcement migration may revoke remaining active NULL rows only after every old writer is gone.

invariants.claim: Only exact epsx-frontend and epsx-admin client values are accepted.
Initial refresh issuance stores the validated client and a new per-login family identifier only after every JWT signature succeeds.
Refresh dependency reads and every fallible JWT signature finish before the destructive rotation transition.

Rotation acquires a transaction-scoped advisory lock keyed by the stored family, conditionally consumes token, wallet, client, family, active state, and expiry, then inserts the exact pre-signed successor in one transaction.
Cross-client, missing-family, and legacy NULL attempts mutate no row and share the invalid-refresh classification used for unknown, expired, revoked, or replayed tokens.
The successor copies the client and family returned by the database transition, and JWT issuance uses the preflight stored client rather than the request DTO.
The rotation chain preserves original authentication time rather than advancing auth_time on every refresh.
Logout and rotation share the transaction-scoped family advisory lock; any historical token revokes only its own active family, while a legacy NULL-family token revokes only itself.
The HTTP refresh request requires an explicit client, emits a closed rotated, not_rotated, rejected, or outcome_unknown marker, is non-cacheable, and never echoes credentials in error bodies.
Frontend and admin BFFs use fixed clients and distinct local cookie names; ambiguous legacy names are clearing-only, and cookies are preserved only for an exact backend-authored not_rotated outcome.

hermeticProof.interpretation: The cumulative auth gate and these pinned commands prove parsing, fixed-client BFF requests, exact JWT-audience rejection, cookie isolation, closed refresh outcomes, non-cacheability, and compiled query shape. They are not PostgreSQL transaction, real-browser, or persistence evidence.

residualStops.claim: No migration in the active core root may be executed until its duplicate baseline-version collision is reconciled.
No disposable PostgreSQL instance has applied this expansion from each supported history or proved that attempted down migration fails atomically without schema or data change.
Populated legacy-row preservation and the later active-NULL revocation cutover are unproved.
PostgreSQL cross-client non-consumption, MVCC single-winner rotation, and deterministic family-lock serialization are unproved.
Rollback on forced successor-insert failure and restart persistence are unproved.
No disposable PostgreSQL instance has applied A1.6 or proven keyed-digest lookup, terminal-state transitions, replay response, and fail-closed startup.

The required drained forced-reauthentication cutover, legacy plaintext reconciliation, persistent secret provisioning, restart persistence, production key rotation, and safe key retirement are unproved and unauthorized.
The shared transaction-scoped family advisory lock has no two-connection PostgreSQL proof for logout-first, rotation-first, stale-token logout, or distinct-family isolation.
Already-issued access tokens remain valid until expiry after logout.
No production issuer, browser, routing, canary, rollback, deployment, database, or service action is authorized by this contract.
